title: CLI/IDE Parity Toggles
description: Operators invoke RootAct from the terminal with yolo, auto, reload, and session-aware modes so the tool feels like a native coding assistant.
value: Reduces friction for users coming from CLI-first agentic coding tools.

title: Project Document Configuration
description: Each project has a rootact.yaml that declares providers, prompts, skills, signatures, and run modes so behavior is reproducible across machines.
value: Team members share one configuration file instead of environment-variable magic.

title: Skill Registry
description: Users register reusable prompt templates and tool wrappers; the harness prepends the selected skill to the intent before planning.
value: Common workflows become one-line invocations.

title: User Signature and Style Registry
description: Users configure a signature profile (author name, title, and a coding quirk such as the Root Knot sentinel) that is injected into generated artifacts.
value: Shipped code carries a consistent human identity stamp.

title: Documentation Mode
description: A run mode that prioritizes writing and updating README, architecture, and audit documents before changing implementation code.
value: Documentation stays in sync with code changes.

title: Git Mode
description: A run mode that stages, commits, and tags changes according to a user-defined commit-message policy and branch rules.
value: Every RootAct session leaves a clean, traceable git history.

title: Prompt Compression and Context Curation
description: The harness ranks project files by relevance and includes whole files within a configurable token budget to maximize model context usage.
value: Large projects fit into limited context windows without manual copy-paste.

title: Artifact Diff Viewer and Change Summary
description: After execution, RootAct attaches a human-readable change summary and file-level diff to the execution report.
value: Reviewers see what changed without calling extra utilities.

title: Dependency-Aware Plan Execution
description: The harness builds a dependency graph from the plan and rejects cyclic plans before execution, ordering steps by dependency.
value: Multi-step changes execute in the correct order.

title: Safety Guardrails and Forbidden-Pattern Filter
description: Every generated artifact is scanned for dangerous patterns such as eval(), exec(), subprocess shell=True, and bare except: blocks.
value: Malicious or careless model output is blocked before it reaches disk.

title: Configuration Validation and Pre-Flight Check
description: RootAct validates rootact.yaml, provider reachability, and prompt file presence before invoking the management model.
value: Fast failure with a clear error instead of a wasted model call.

title: Intent History Log and Observability Sink
description: Every intent, plan, and artifact is recorded with SHA-256 checksums and provenance so sessions are auditable.
value: Users can reconstruct why a change was made and what model produced it.

title: Automated Test Case Generation for Edge Cases
description: RootAct generates boundary, empty-input, numeric-limit, and fallback test cases from keywords in the intent.
value: Edge-case coverage is generated, not forgotten.

title: Plan Replay
description: A saved plan can be re-executed later, optionally against a different provider, for reproducibility and regression testing.
value: Expensive reasoning can be reused and verified.

title: Approval Queue CLI
description: In non-yolo modes, RootAct queues destructive or risky steps and prompts the operator for approval before continuing.
value: Prevents accidental overwrites or deletions.

title: Self-Test Benchmark Mode
description: RootAct runs a suite of internal checks and provider benchmarks to verify installation and baseline performance.
value: Confidence that the tool is correctly configured before real work.

title: Code Review Mode
description: RootAct reads an existing file or diff and produces a structured review checklist with severity ratings.
value: Consistent, reproducible first-pass reviews.

title: Session Store and Reload
description: Conversations, plans, and partial results persist across process restarts; users can resume a session by name.
value: Multi-day tasks survive reboots and crashes.

title: Multi-Provider Capability Routing
description: RootAct routes steps to the cheapest or most capable configured provider based on capability hints, not hardcoded names.
value: Mix local and frontier models without changing plan logic.

title: Provider Retry and Backoff
description: Transient provider failures (timeouts, 5xx, 429) trigger exponential-backoff retries before surfacing a final error.
value: Brief provider hiccups do not kill a long-running task.

title: Streaming Completions
description: Optionally stream provider responses so users see progress for long reasoning or code-generation tasks.
value: Improves perceived responsiveness.

title: Memory Arena for Long-Horizon Context
description: Important facts, decisions, and constraints extracted during a session are stored in a structured memory arena and replayed into context.
value: Models remember what matters even after context compression.

title: Quality Scorecard
description: RootAct scores each execution report on test coverage, lint cleanliness, diff size, and provenance completeness.
value: Objective quality signal for every RootAct run.

title: Rollback and Checkpoint Engine
description: RootAct can snapshot the working directory before execution and roll back to the snapshot on failure.
value: Failed model changes are cheap to undo.

title: Built-In Model Fine-Tuning
description: RootAct would train custom LoRA adapters on user projects.
reason: Out of scope for a public, model-agnostic coding tool; training belongs in the provider or a separate training harness.

title: Native Graphical User Interface
description: RootAct would ship a built-in desktop GUI.
reason: CLI-first keeps the tool portable and scriptable; web/desktop front ends can be built as separate consumers of the API/harness.

title: Configuration-Driven Project Templates
description: Users scaffold a new project with rootact init --template <name> --provider <name>, producing rootact.yaml, prompts, starter source/tests/README, and an installed skill.
value: First-time users go from install to a working project in one command.

title: OpenAPI Client Generation
description: RootAct reads an OpenAPI 3 JSON/YAML specification and emits an httpx-based Python client class with typed methods for each operation.
value: Turns an API contract into working client code in one command.
